name: stylesmith
description: One click for a complete look in VS Code and your terminal: themes, pixel icons and editor settings that belong together, checked for contrast and color blindness, with a matching Nerd Font if you want one. One click to undo it. Stylesmith does not modify VS Code installation files, apart from removing changes made by Stylesmith 1.x.

stylesmith.fonts.enabled.markdownDescription: Use a Nerd Font in the editor and terminal, set through VS Code’s font settings. The font must be installed; Stylesmith can install it for your user account, after you confirm.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Needs the JetBrainsMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you.
Needs the BlexMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you.
Needs the ShureTechMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you.
Needs the DepartureMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you.
Needs the GeistMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Geist Mono.
Needs the SpaceMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Space Mono.
Needs the AtkynsonMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, designed by the Braille Institute for readers with low vision.
Needs the MonaspiceXe Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Monaspace Xenon, a slab-serif monospace.
Needs the RecMonoCasual Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Recursive Mono, in its casual style.
Needs the MartianMono Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. Based on Martian Mono.
Needs the 3270 Nerd Font family installed; Stylesmith can install it for you. A recreation of the IBM 3270 terminal font, in Regular only.
stylesmith.fonts.family.markdownDescription: Which font family to use. It must be installed on your system: install it yourself, or let Stylesmith install it for your user account from the Stylesmith menu, after you confirm. The setting takes effect immediately.

stylesmith.problems.enabled.markdownDescription: Show diagnostics inline with VS Code editor decorations. Works without Enable and updates live.

stylesmith.problems.minimumSeverity.description: The least severe kind of problem the Problem Lens shows.

stylesmith.problems.inlineMessages.description: Show the problem's message at the end of its line.

stylesmith.problems.gutterIcons.description: Show a pixel icon in the gutter: a square with an X for errors, a triangle for warnings, a circle for info.

stylesmith.problems.statusBar.description: Show the problem on the cursor's line in the status bar, next to the line and column numbers.

stylesmith.problems.errorSignal.description: When the number of errors in your files goes up, show the new count in the status bar for a moment, on the error background. It shows once, at most every two seconds.

stylesmith.terminal.failSignal.markdownDescription: When a command in the integrated terminal fails, show its exit code in the status bar for a moment, on the error background. It shows once, at most every two seconds; a command stopped with Ctrl+C doesn't count. Needs VS Code's shell integration (`terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled`, on by default for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell).

stylesmith.statusbar.description: Show the Stylesmith button in the status bar. It opens a menu with presets, supported effects and fonts.

stylesmith.undoHighlight.description: After an undo, tint the lines it changed for a moment, so you can see what came back. Uses the stylesmith.undoHighlightBackground theme color.

stylesmith.saveReceipt.description: After a manual save (not an auto-save), note it at the end of the cursor’s line for two seconds, like a terminal log: “▸ saved 14:02:11”. Uses the stylesmith.saveReceiptForeground theme color.

stylesmith.effects.smoothCursor.description: Use VS Code’s native smooth caret animation and smooth cursor blinking.

stylesmith.effects.currentLine.description: Highlight the current editor line using VS Code’s native line highlight.

stylesmith.effects.bracketGuides.description: Show VS Code’s native active bracket pair guides.

stylesmith.effects.compactLayout.description: Use compact layout density where supported by this VS Code version.

stylesmith.effects.blockCursor.description: Use a block cursor in the editor, like a terminal of the 1970s and 80s, with VS Code’s native editor.cursorStyle setting.

stylesmith.effects.blockTerminalCursor.description: Use VS Code’s native blinking block terminal cursor.

stylesmith.effects.dimUnfocused.description: Dim editors and terminals that don't have focus, with VS Code’s native accessibility.dimUnfocused setting, so the one you're working in stands out.

stylesmith.effects.readableTerminal.description: Raise the minimum contrast of terminal text to 7:1 (WCAG AAA), with VS Code’s native terminal.integrated.minimumContrastRatio. VS Code then adjusts any terminal color below that ratio, including colors that programs choose.

stylesmith.effects.neonBlocks.markdownDeprecationMessage: Removed in Stylesmith 2.0. Use `stylesmith.effects.bracketGuides` instead; Stylesmith moves your value there and removes this setting.

stylesmith.effects.classicLayout.markdownDeprecationMessage: Removed in Stylesmith 2.0. Use `stylesmith.effects.compactLayout` instead; Stylesmith moves your value there and removes this setting.

stylesmith.effects.retroTerminalCursor.markdownDeprecationMessage: Removed in Stylesmith 2.0. Use `stylesmith.effects.blockTerminalCursor` instead; Stylesmith moves your value there and removes this setting.

colors.description: Background of the lines an undo changed, shown briefly when stylesmith.undoHighlight is on.
Text of the note shown briefly after a manual save, when stylesmith.saveReceipt is on.

scripts.format: prettier --write src scripts site extras eslint.config.mjs tsconfig*.json package.json "*.md"
scripts.format:check: prettier --check src scripts site extras eslint.config.mjs tsconfig*.json package.json "*.md"
scripts.test:browser: npm run compile && tsc -p tsconfig.browser.json && node --test "out/test-browser/**/*.test.js"

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Stylesmith uses its built-in assets and VS Code APIs, and downloads a font only when you ask it to install one; it does not load code or configuration from the workspace.
